nodes.label: The zram-generator default `min(ram / 2, 4096)` was introduced in v1.1.0 (2021-11-16) as a numerically identical replacement for `zram-fraction`=0.5 times `max-zram-size`=4096

nodes.label: A zram device's disksize is uncompressed capacity, not memory: mem_used_total runs about 1.334x compr_data_size, so an uncapped 3973 MiB device reaches ~2.59 GiB at the kernel's 2:1 planning ratio and ~5.18 GiB incompressible

nodes.label: Running zswap on top of zram is redundant: the Arch kernel doc states that if zswap remains enabled it will prevent zram from being used effectively, so the host's zswap.enabled=0 is the correct layering

nodes.label: 0.5 sits at the top of upstream's documented recommended 0.1-0.5 fraction band, so 51% of RAM is defensible as capacity; the defect is the missing cap, not the size

nodes.label: The 1940 MiB cap was chosen because it is non-binding at the host's observed 4.2x ratio, binds only at the kernel's conservative 2:1, and bites solely in the incompressible case — non-binding in normal operation, binding exactly when the kernel is already in trouble
